        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:

          type: string
          minLength: 1

          pattern: '.*\S.*'

        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored and returned value is a '+'
            followed by 8 to 15 digits (e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes

          maxLength: 20

All tests pass — the suite contains a single acceptance test (`coreCountsNamesakes`), and the full `./mvnw test` run is `BUILD SUCCESS`.

## Summary

I implemented `namesakeCount` on owner creation. Because the acceptance test reads the value back via `GET /api/owners/{id}` (not just the create response), the count is computed at create time and **persisted** on the owner, mirroring how the existing `customerCode`/`householdId` derived fields work.

Changes:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added `namesakeCount` as a `readOnly` `int32` property (min 0) to the `Owner` response schema. This regenerates `OwnerDto` with a `namesakeCount` accessor during the build.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a persisted `Integer namesakeCount` field (`@Column(name = "namesake_count")`) with getter/setter. MapStruct auto-maps it into `OwnerDto` by name, so it's returned on both the create response and later GETs.

3. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, before saving, count existing owners whose `firstName` **and** `lastName` match the new owner case-insensitively (via `findAllOwners()`, consistent with the existing duplicate/customer-code logic), and set it on the entity.

4. **Schema files** (`db/hsqldb`, `db/h2`, `db/mysql`, `db/postgres`) — added the `namesake_count` column. Tests run on the `hsqldb` profile; the others are updated for consistency.

The test creates two owners sharing `firstName`+`lastName` (different addresses so no household 409), and the second reports `namesakeCount = 1`, which passes.
